source.title: C-Flat++: Towards a More Efficient and Powerful Framework for Continual Learning
source.authors: Wei Li; Hang-Jie Yuan; Zi-Xiang Zhao; Yi-Fan Zhu; Ao-Jun Lu; Guodong Du; Ya-Nan Sun; Tao Feng

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses loss-landscape flatness as a training method for continual learning and reports its performance. It does not measure train–test gaps or test the claim versions; its sharpness measurements are related findings but do not establish that sharpness tracks those gaps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports continual-learning accuracy and efficiency results for C-Flat and C-Flat++, but these evaluate the proposed methods rather than the claim versions. It also reports Hessian eigenvalue and trace comparisons; these measure curvature, not train–test gaps.
record.test_reason: The study uses flatness to design continual-learning optimizers and evaluates their accuracy, efficiency and curvature. It does not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance against train–test gaps, as V7 requires, or test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that C-Flat improves continual-learning performance, curvature analyses indicate flatter minima, and C-Flat++ reduces computational overhead through selective updates. Their claims of consistent improvement have exceptions: Table II includes accuracy declines, and Section IV-H reports greater forgetting in four of seven scenarios.
record.recipe_differences: Continual-learning optimization using C-Flat or C-Flat++, rather than the claim versions’ interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that CL accuracy varies across datasets, incremental settings, and baseline methods; its C-Flat ablation varies λ and ρ and reports that C-Flat is not oversensitive within a reasonable hyperparameter range.

fits_no_version.finding: For MEMO on CIFAR-100 B0 Inc10, C-Flat and C-Flat++ have lower maximum Hessian eigenvalues and empirical-Fisher trace estimates than vanilla SGD at epochs 50 and 150.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: C-Flat and C-Flat++ reduce these curvature measures in the tested continual-learning setting.

record.problems: The reported curvature comparisons do not measure train–test gaps. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported Hessian eigenvalue and trace values.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported continual-learning accuracy, speed, transfer, or ablation results are included: those evaluate the proposed continual-learning methods and do not measure a claim version or the train–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including interactions with data size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All eight rows are related method-evaluation results rather than evidence for the listed versions. Lower curvature alongside better continual-learning test accuracy does not establish V7's relationship with train–test gaps. The omitted accuracy, transfer, efficiency and ablation results are declared in rows_left_out and do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and momentum on held-out benchmarks.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its relationship to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
